---
title: "slenderpy"
subtitle: "Simulation of slender structures: overhead line cables and beams"
---

slenderpy computes the static shape and the time-domain response of slender
structures, suspended cables and tensioned beams, under user-defined loads
such as wind. It is developed for overhead power lines, where these
vibrations drive conductor fatigue.

- **Cable**: catenary, parabolic and elastic closed forms; the static shape
  under any load; the nonlinear dynamics of [Lee and Perkins
  (1992)](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF00045648); natural
  frequencies.
- **Beam**: Euler-Bernoulli beam with a constant bending stiffness or a
  Bouc-Wen hysteretic law, approximate or exact curvature, static and dynamic.
- **Forces**: gravity, point excitation, wind drag with a constant or
  turbulent wind; any force can be written as a plain function.
- **Fatigue**: rainflow cycle counting at a distance from a support.
- **Stockbridge dampers** (experimental), and the former API kept in
  [`slenderpy.legacy`](legacy.qmd).

## Installation

```bash
python -m pip install "slenderpy @ git+https://github.com/rte-france/pallas-slenderpy"
```

or, with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), `uv add "slenderpy @ git+https://github.com/rte-france/pallas-slenderpy"`.

## A first look

A 400 m span under its weight, then under a steady 25 m/s wind:

::: {#995155cf .cell execution_count=1}
``` {.python .cell-code}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

from slenderpy.cable import dynamic
from slenderpy.cable.static import shape
from slenderpy.components import Conductor, Span
from slenderpy.force.wind import ConstantWind, WindDrag

conductor = Conductor(mass=1.571, diameter=0.0313, axial_stiffness=3.76e07)
span = Span(length=400.0, tension=3.7e04)
x, y, z = dynamic.equilibrium(conductor, span, 201)

drag = WindDrag(diameter=conductor.diameter, wind=ConstantWind(25.0))
zeros = np.zeros_like(x)
windy = shape.solve(conductor, span, *drag(x, 0.0, y, z, zeros, zeros), 201)

fig, (side, top) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 3.5))
side.plot(x, z, "k", label="weight only")
side.plot(windy[0], windy[2], label="25 m/s wind")
top.plot(windy[0], windy[1], c="C0")
side.set(title="side view", xlabel="x (m)", ylabel="z (m)")
top.set(title="plan view", xlabel="x (m)", ylabel="y (m)")
side.legend()
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
